name: thinking-state
useWhen: The agent is between turns and the user has nothing to look at. Smallest honest signal: work is happening, no detail claimed.

name: thinking-reasoning
useWhen: Reasoning is long enough that showing it all costs attention, but hiding it costs trust. Collapsed by default, expandable for the user who wants the chain.

name: orbs
useWhen: A thinking state that shares a chat line with an avatar and must read as alive at 20–64px instead of as a stalled spinner.

name: web-search
useWhen: The agent left the conversation to fetch sources, and the user should see the query and the hits before the answer arrives.

name: file-diff
useWhen: The agent edited code and the user must approve or audit the exact lines — inline `+`/`-` with the surrounding context, not a prose summary.

name: image-generation
useWhen: Generation takes seconds and the layout must reserve the final image's box now, so the transcript does not jump when it resolves.

name: text-response
useWhen: The finished, non-streamed reply: markdown, bold, inline code, sane spacing. The default block every other one falls back to.

name: streaming-text
useWhen: Tokens arrive over a socket and perceived latency matters more than a clean paint.

name: inline-citations
useWhen: The answer makes factual claims and each one needs an attributable source at the exact sentence, not a link dump at the end.

name: code-block
useWhen: Agent output is code the user will copy — filename header, highlighting, copy button, no accidental markdown mangling.

name: task-list
useWhen: A multi-step plan runs longer than one turn and the user needs to see what is done, running, and still queued.

name: data-table
useWhen: Structured tool output belongs in rows and columns; a markdown table would lose alignment and overflow on mobile.

name: comparison-table
useWhen: The agent's answer is a recommendation between options and the user should be able to check the criteria side by side.

name: ai-agent-input
useWhen: The composer needs agent affordances — multiline, submit-on-enter, attachments — and a plain `Textarea` would need all of it rebuilt.

name: apple-hello-effect
useWhen: A landing or splash screen needs one memorable opening beat, and a handwritten "hello" drawing itself earns more attention than a fade-in headline.

name: brand-assets-menu
useWhen: Press and partners keep asking for your logo files. Right-click the mark, copy the SVG, or jump to the brand guidelines.

name: chevrons-up-down-icon
useWhen: A sort control or select trigger where the icon should morph between up and down instead of swapping frames.

name: code-block-command
useWhen: Docs show an install snippet across npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun, and the package-manager tabs plus copy button should already work.

name: consent-manager
useWhen: You need a cookie banner that respects the design instead of a vendor widget bolted on top — GDPR categories with per-category opt-in.

name: copy-button
useWhen: Any copyable value where the button must confirm the copy landed and reset itself afterwards.

name: dot-grid-spotlight
useWhen: A hero or section background that should react to the pointer without becoming the subject of the page.

name: elastic-slider
useWhen: A volume or intensity control that should feel rubbery at the ends, so hitting the limit is felt and not just displayed.

name: fluid-gradient-text
useWhen: A headline where the gradient follows the cursor across the words — interactive emphasis instead of a static gradient fill.

name: github-contributions
useWhen: A developer profile or team page proving activity over time, using the grid everyone already knows how to read.

name: github-stars
useWhen: An open-source project page where the live star count is the social proof, fetched rather than hard-coded.

name: glow-card-grid
useWhen: A feature grid where hovering one card should light its border and leave neighbours calm.

name: haptic
useWhen: A mobile web app where confirmations should be felt, not only seen, on devices that support the Vibration API.

name: icon-swap
useWhen: An icon changes meaning mid-interaction (play/pause, copy/copied) and should scale-blur across instead of popping.

name: line-nav
useWhen: A long vertical nav where the active item must stay findable — its marker extends and it scrolls itself into view on mount.

name: logos-carousel
useWhen: More customer logos than fit the row: cycle them column by column in a staggered wave rather than scrolling a marquee.

name: middle-truncation
useWhen: File paths, wallet addresses, or hashes where the tail identifies the item, so trailing `…` would destroy the information.

name: mobius-loop-icon
useWhen: A looping or "always on" concept needs a mark that morphs between circle and infinity rather than a static glyph.

name: react-wheel-picker
useWhen: A mobile web flow where a native-feeling iOS wheel beats a dropdown for dates, times, or durations.

name: scroll-fade-effect
useWhen: A scroll container whose hard cut-off makes it look broken — the fade signals there is more without adding a scrollbar.

name: share-menu
useWhen: An article or product page where sharing must cover copy-link, X, LinkedIn, and the native share sheet in one control.

name: shimmering-text
useWhen: One label ("New", "Pro", a loading heading) should draw the eye with a slow sweep and no layout impact.

name: slide-to-unlock
useWhen: A consequential action where a click is too cheap and a confirm dialog is too heavy — the gesture is the confirmation.

name: spinning-circular-text
useWhen: A badge, seal, or scroll cue where text on a rotating circle carries the brand mark.

name: spotlight-logo
useWhen: The logomark itself is the interaction: highlight tracks the cursor, press morphs the paths, reduced motion respected.

name: testimonial
useWhen: One quote, quietly presented, when the section is not about testimonials.

name: testimonial-2
useWhen: A quote that must be verifiable — author, role, and a link back to the original post.

name: testimonial-spotlight
useWhen: One customer story deserves editorial weight and should not sit in a grid of equals.

name: testimonials-marquee
useWhen: You have thirty quotes and want the volume itself to read as proof, in a strip that keeps moving.

name: text-flip
useWhen: A hero headline that names several audiences or use cases by rotating the last word.

name: theme-switcher
useWhen: Three-way light/dark/system choice that must be explicit, because a two-state toggle cannot express "system".

name: theme-toggle-effect
useWhen: Theme switching should feel deliberate — the new theme wipes in from the button using the View Transitions API.

name: timescale
useWhen: Milestones plotted against a real time axis, where the *gaps* between events carry meaning a plain list would flatten.

name: toc-minimap
useWhen: Long-form docs where a full table of contents costs too much width but the reader still needs position and jump targets.

name: twemoji
useWhen: Emoji appear in user-generated content and must render identically on Windows, Android, and iOS.

name: work-experience-component
useWhen: A CV or about page with roles, dates, and nested projects that should collapse instead of running to three screens.

name: pdf-viewer
useWhen: Users must read the source PDF next to extracted data — sending them to a download breaks the review loop.

name: docx-viewer
useWhen: Word files arrive from clients and must be readable in-app without a Microsoft round trip.

name: docx-editor
useWhen: Users have to change the Word document itself and hand it back, not just comment on it.

name: xlsx-viewer
useWhen: A spreadsheet needs inspecting with its sheets and formatting intact, before anything is imported.

name: xlsx-editor
useWhen: Cell values must be corrected in place — typically fixing what an extraction model got wrong.

name: pptx-viewer
useWhen: Slide decks are part of the intake and users need to page through them without PowerPoint.

name: csv-tsv-viewer
useWhen: A delimited file needs previewing as a table before import, so bad delimiters and headers surface early.

name: document-viewer-sidebar
useWhen: A long document needs page thumbnails and jump targets, because scrolling 200 pages is not navigation.

name: document-splits
useWhen: One scanned batch holds many logical documents and a human must confirm where each one starts.

name: file-upload
useWhen: Intake is document-heavy: many files, real formats, per-file progress and errors.

name: file-thumbnail
useWhen: A list of uploads is unusable as filenames alone — users recognise documents by how they look.

name: file-system
useWhen: Documents live in folders users browse, move, and organise, rather than a flat list.

name: schema-builder
useWhen: Users define what to extract themselves, so the product does not need a developer for every new document type.

name: bounding-box-citations
useWhen: Every extracted value must point back to the exact place on the page — the difference between an audit trail and a guess.

name: e-signature
useWhen: A document flow ends in a signature and a third-party signing vendor would be too much machinery.

name: blocks
useWhen: You need the whole document-agent shell — viewer, sidebar, extraction panel — arranged and wired.

name: blocks
useWhen: The full citation review screen: extracted fields on one side, highlighted source on the other.

name: blocks
useWhen: Split review for spreadsheets, where the boundary is a sheet or row range rather than a page.

name: blocks
useWhen: A focused single-purpose screen: drop a PDF, see it, act on it. Good first screen of a document product.

name: blocks
useWhen: The editing screen around the DOCX editor, including file state and save actions.

name: blocks
useWhen: The complete signing screen: document, signer fields, and confirmation.

name: accordion
useWhen: Sections open and close often enough that a jumpy height transition becomes the thing users notice.

name: ask-user-questions
useWhen: An agent or wizard must ask a real question mid-flow: preset options, a skip path, and a free-text answer, without a modal.

name: badge
useWhen: Status labels sit beside these controls and stock shadcn badges would look flat next to them.

name: button
useWhen: The primary action should confirm the press physically — the baseline this whole set is tuned against.

name: card
useWhen: A container that has to hold the set's surface treatment, so nested controls do not look pasted on.

name: chat-message
useWhen: A conversation surface built from the same system as the rest of the app, instead of an imported chat kit.

name: checkbox-group
useWhen: Several related settings are toggled in one sitting and each change must register instantly.

name: color-picker
useWhen: Users pick a brand or label colour and need to see the result while dragging, not after releasing.

name: dialog
useWhen: A modal that must not feel abrupt — it should arrive from and return to its trigger.

name: dropdown
useWhen: Grouped actions behind one trigger, with a highlight that travels between items rather than blinking.

name: input-copy
useWhen: An API key, install command, or invite URL is shown to be copied, so the field and the copy action belong together.

name: input-group
useWhen: Related fields (currency + amount, protocol + host) read as one control instead of three inputs in a row.

name: input-message
useWhen: A chat composer with send and attachments, matching the rest of the system's motion.

name: radio-group
useWhen: An exclusive choice where the selection should visibly move between options, making the swap legible.

name: select
useWhen: A single choice from a longer list — roles, modes, environments — inside a settings surface.

name: slider
useWhen: A value is tuned by feel, not typed, and the handle must track the pointer without lag.

name: switch
useWhen: An instant-effect setting where the toggle itself is the confirmation, since there is no save button.

name: table
useWhen: A small table inside a settings or detail panel, where a full data grid would be overkill.

name: tabs
useWhen: Primary section switching where the indicator should carry the eye across.

name: tabs-subtle
useWhen: Secondary switching inside a panel that already has tabs above it, so the two levels stay distinguishable.

name: thinking-indicator
useWhen: Background work is running and the app needs a house-style waiting state instead of a foreign spinner.

name: thinking-steps
useWhen: The wait is long enough that the user should see *which* step is running, not just that something is.

name: tooltip
useWhen: Dense controls need labels on hover, with delays tuned so passing the cursor over a toolbar does not flash.

name: surfaces
useWhen: Read before mixing this set into an existing app — it defines the elevation and background rules everything else assumes.

name: scrollbars
useWhen: Default scrollbars break the surface treatment in panels and dropdowns.

name: motion
useWhen: You extend the set with your own components and need the same spring constants, or you must audit reduced-motion behaviour.

name: accordion
useWhen: You need an accordion with height-auto animation done correctly.

name: blur-up-image
useWhen: You need images that resolve from a blurred placeholder into the full photo.

name: collapsible-banner
useWhen: You need a banner that collapses to its title or dismisses entirely.

name: command-palette
useWhen: You need a command palette whose results reorder live as you type.

name: context-menu
useWhen: You need a right-click menu that opens from the pointer, not the corner.

name: copy-button
useWhen: You need a copy interaction that locks its width and reverts after a timeout.

name: drawer
useWhen: You need a side panel that keeps its scroll position and state.

name: dropdown
useWhen: You need a dropdown menu whose active highlight travels between items.

name: expanding-search
useWhen: You need a search icon that expands into a focused field.

name: filter-grid
useWhen: You need a grid that rearranges on filter instead of blinking.

name: floating-label
useWhen: You need form labels that float out of the way instead of disappearing on focus.

name: hide-on-scroll
useWhen: You need a toolbar that hides on scroll down and yields to content.

name: hold-to-confirm
useWhen: You need a hold gesture that guards a destructive action from accidental clicks.

name: icon-morph
useWhen: You need a play/pause or menu/close icon that morphs between states instead of swapping.

name: inline-validation
useWhen: You need inline form error messages that don't shove the layout around.

name: lightbox
useWhen: You need an image lightbox that zooms in and returns to its origin on close.

name: like-burst
useWhen: You need an optimistic like/favorite animation that stays correct under rapid taps.

name: live-activity
useWhen: You need a compact, persistent indicator for ongoing system work.

name: load-more
useWhen: You need infinite-scroll loading that starts before the user hits the bottom.

name: loading-button
useWhen: You need a submit button that shows a loading state without resizing.

name: logo-marquee
useWhen: You need a logo marquee that pauses when the user looks at it.

name: long-press
useWhen: You need a long-press gesture confirmed by hold time and cancelled by any interruption.

name: modal
useWhen: You need a modal with backdrop, scroll lock, and focus trap handled correctly.

name: new-items-pill
useWhen: You need a "new content" pill that appears without stealing the user's scroll position.

name: otp-input
useWhen: You need a one-time-code input with auto-advance, paste, and error recovery.

name: pagination
useWhen: You need pagination where the visible window moves without the row jumping.

name: password-strength
useWhen: You need a strength meter that reads segment by segment as the user types.

name: poll-results
useWhen: You need poll or vote result bars where the winner animates in last.

name: popover
useWhen: You need a popover that knows its trigger origin and flips on collision.

name: presence-avatars
useWhen: You need an avatar stack that animates as people join or leave.

name: press-depth
useWhen: You need buttons that visually confirm a press landed.

name: progress-bar
useWhen: You need a progress bar that moves from indeterminate to determinate cleanly.

name: reading-progress
useWhen: You need a reading-progress indicator showing how much content is left.

name: reorder-list
useWhen: You need a drag-to-reorder list where the gap itself is the drop target.

name: ripple
useWhen: You need pointer-origin touch feedback on tap targets.

name: scroll-spy
useWhen: You need navigation that highlights the section actually in view.

name: segmented-control
useWhen: You need a segmented control where the thumb slides and the label inverts through it.

name: show-more
useWhen: You need a "show more" toggle that animates height without reflowing text.

name: skeleton-swap
useWhen: You need skeleton loaders that swap to content with zero layout shift.

name: slider-detents
useWhen: You need a slider with snap points the user can feel.

name: snap-carousel
useWhen: You need a carousel where momentum scrolling lands cleanly on a slide.

name: sortable-table
useWhen: You need a table where rows animate to their new sorted order.

name: sticky-header
useWhen: You need a header that condenses as the user scrolls down.

name: streaming-text
useWhen: You need token-by-token streaming text with a caret, like an LLM response.

name: swipe-deck
useWhen: You need a swipeable card stack, like a decision deck.

name: tabs
useWhen: You need tabs sharing one animated indicator.

name: tag-input
useWhen: You need a tag input where Enter adds and backspace highlights before removing.

name: task-steps
useWhen: You need a step list that narrates ongoing background work.

name: text-reveal
useWhen: You need text that reveals in reading order.

name: tooltip-group
useWhen: You need tooltips that delay once, then show instantly for the rest of the group.

name: tree-view
useWhen: You need a tree view whose disclosure works with arrow keys.

name: typing-indicator
useWhen: You need a "someone is typing" indicator for chat or collaborative UIs.

name: value-flash
useWhen: You need numbers that flash or highlight when they change.

name: wizard-steps
useWhen: You need a multi-step wizard whose transitions know forward from back.

name: android
useWhen: An Android screenshot needs a device frame so it reads as a real app rather than a floating image.

name: animated-beam
useWhen: An integration or architecture diagram must show that data actually flows between two nodes.

name: animated-circular-progress-bar
useWhen: A single percentage is the headline number — usage, score, completion — and a bar would read as secondary.

name: animated-gradient-text
useWhen: A launch pill or badge above the hero headline needs to catch the eye before the headline does.

name: animated-grid-pattern
useWhen: A section background should feel alive without competing with the copy — cells fade in and out slowly.

name: animated-list
useWhen: You are demonstrating a live feed (notifications, events, orders) and items must enter in sequence, not all at once.

name: animated-shiny-text
useWhen: A small label needs a slow sweep of light to look interactive, typically a "What's new" link.

name: animated-theme-toggler
useWhen: Theme switching should be a moment, using View Transitions to wipe the new theme in from the button.

name: aurora-text
useWhen: One or two words in the hero headline carry the whole brand colour, with the gradient in motion.

name: avatar-circles
useWhen: Social proof near the call to action: overlapping faces plus a count, in the width of a button.

name: backlight
useWhen: A product video or screenshot should look lit from behind, lifting it off a dark section.

name: bento-grid
useWhen: Features differ in weight and a uniform three-column grid would flatten them into equals.

name: blur-fade
useWhen: Sections should resolve as the user scrolls to them, giving a long page rhythm instead of one flat reveal.

name: border-beam
useWhen: A single card — the recommended plan, the featured feature — must be the one thing that moves on screen.

name: code-comparison
useWhen: The pitch is "before and after our tool", and the diff itself is the argument.

name: comic-text
useWhen: A playful brand needs a headline with comic-book weight and impact, not a standard type ramp.

name: confetti
useWhen: A genuine milestone lands — signup complete, first deploy — and the moment should be celebrated once, not on every click.

name: cool-mode
useWhen: A single element gets a particle burst on click, for a playful surface where delight beats restraint.

name: dia-text-reveal
useWhen: A headline should arrive under a sweeping colour band and settle into the theme foreground.

name: dock
useWhen: A small icon toolbar should feel macOS-native, magnifying under the cursor.

name: dot-pattern
useWhen: A section needs texture rather than a flat colour, and dots read quieter than a grid.

name: dotted-map
useWhen: You claim global coverage and need a lightweight SVG world map instead of a mapping library.

name: file-tree
useWhen: Docs or a landing page must show project structure, and an indented code block would be unreadable.

name: flickering-grid
useWhen: A technical or infrastructure product needs a background that suggests activity and machines.

name: glare-hover
useWhen: A card should catch light diagonally on hover — glass-like, done with CSS only, no extra keyframes.

name: globe
useWhen: An interactive globe with markers, when the claim is worldwide reach and a flat map undersells it.

name: glyph-matrix
useWhen: A canvas background of shifting glyphs, for a developer or security product where "data moving" is the mood.

name: grid-pattern
useWhen: A static blueprint-style grid behind a section — the calm baseline the animated variants build on.

name: hero-video-dialog
useWhen: The demo video must not autoplay in the hero, but the thumbnail should open it in a proper dialog.

name: hexagon-pattern
useWhen: A background with more structure than dots, for a technical or scientific feel.

name: highlighter
useWhen: A phrase in a paragraph is the point and needs a hand-drawn marker stroke instead of a `<mark>` block.

name: hyper-text
useWhen: A heading should scramble into place on hover or on view, for a technical brand.

name: icon-cloud
useWhen: You support dozens of integrations and a rotating sphere of logos shows the breadth a list would bury.

name: interactive-grid-pattern
useWhen: The background should respond to the pointer, making an otherwise static section feel touchable.

name: interactive-hover-button
useWhen: The primary call to action should transform on hover, not merely darken.

name: iphone
useWhen: A mobile screenshot needs an iPhone frame with correct proportions and notch.

name: kinetic-text
useWhen: A variable font is loaded and hovering the headline should shift character weight — typography as the interaction.

name: lens
useWhen: Detail matters in an image (a dashboard screenshot, a product photo) and users should magnify it in place.

name: light-rays
useWhen: A dark hero needs directional light so the composition has a source instead of a flat gradient.

name: line-shadow-text
useWhen: A headline needs an offset line shadow for editorial weight, with an animated stroke.

name: magic-card
useWhen: A grid of cards where the border should follow the cursor, so hover targets are unmistakable.

name: marquee
useWhen: Logos or testimonials outnumber the available width and infinite scroll beats a cramped grid.

name: meteors
useWhen: A dark section needs slow diagonal motion in the background — space-themed, cheap to run.

name: morphing-text
useWhen: One headline word cycles through several values and letters should melt between them rather than cut.

name: neon-gradient-card
useWhen: A card must glow hard against a dark background — highest-attention treatment in the set.

name: noise-texture
useWhen: Flat gradients band on real displays; an SVG turbulence layer removes the plastic look.

name: number-ticker
useWhen: A stats row should count up when it scrolls into view, so the numbers get read instead of skipped.

name: orbiting-circles
useWhen: Your product sits at the centre of an ecosystem, and orbiting logos say that faster than a diagram.

name: particles
useWhen: A hero needs ambient depth that reacts to the pointer without a WebGL dependency.

name: pixel-image
useWhen: An image should resolve from pixelation, turning a plain asset into a reveal.

name: pointer
useWhen: A demo area needs a custom cursor to signal "this is interactive, try it".

name: progressive-blur
useWhen: Scrollable content must fade under a sticky header or toolbar instead of being cut off hard.

name: pulsating-button
useWhen: One call to action must be found without reading — waitlist, live event, limited offer.

name: rainbow-button
useWhen: The primary button carries the brand's colour range, when a single accent colour looks too plain.

name: retro-grid
useWhen: A synthwave horizon grid, for a brand that leans deliberately retro.

name: ripple
useWhen: Concentric rings behind a centred hero element, suggesting broadcast or reach.

name: ripple-button
useWhen: A button should show where it was clicked, Material-style, on touch-heavy surfaces.

name: safari
useWhen: A web app screenshot needs a browser chrome frame so it reads as a real product, with your URL in the bar.

name: scroll-based-velocity
useWhen: A text strip should speed up and reverse with scroll direction, tying motion to the reader's own input.

name: scroll-progress
useWhen: Long-form content needs a reading indicator so the length is visible from the first screen.

name: shimmer-button
useWhen: A premium call to action with a light sweep — quieter than pulsating, louder than a solid fill.

name: shine-border
useWhen: A card border should shine periodically, marking it as featured without the constant motion of a beam.

name: shiny-button
useWhen: A secondary action still needs polish, but must not compete with the primary one.

name: smooth-cursor
useWhen: A portfolio or agency site replaces the system cursor with a lagging, springy one.

name: sparkles-text
useWhen: A word should sparkle — typically the AI or "magic" feature name in the hero.

name: spinning-text
useWhen: A circular text badge rotates around a mark or a scroll cue.

name: striped-pattern
useWhen: A diagonal striped background for a section that needs separation without a hard divider.

name: terminal
useWhen: A CLI product should show its own output typing itself out — the most honest demo a CLI can give.

name: text-3d-flip
useWhen: Letters flip in 3D on hover with a stagger, for a playful headline.

name: text-animate
useWhen: You need one text-entrance API covering fade, slide, blur, and stagger, instead of four components.

name: text-reveal
useWhen: A statement should reveal word by word as the user scrolls it, forcing a slower read.

name: tweet-card
useWhen: Real posts are the testimonials, and the embedded X widget would cost a third-party script and a layout shift.

name: typing-animation
useWhen: A headline or prompt example should type itself, mimicking someone using the product.

name: video-text
useWhen: Video plays inside the letterforms of a headline, for a bold single-word hero.

name: warp-background
useWhen: A section background should warp toward a vanishing point, suggesting speed.

name: word-rotate
useWhen: The headline names several audiences and the last word cycles cleanly between them.

name: client
useWhen: First step in a new App Router project — server, client, and middleware clients set up so sessions survive server components.

name: password-based-auth
useWhen: You need the full email/password surface, including the reset and update flows people forget until launch.

name: social-auth
useWhen: Sign-in should be one click via an OAuth provider, with the callback route already handled.

name: dropzone
useWhen: Uploads go to Supabase Storage and you want bucket paths, progress, and errors wired rather than re-derived.

name: current-user-avatar
useWhen: The header avatar must reflect the signed-in user without you plumbing the session down to it.

name: realtime-avatar-stack
useWhen: Users should see who else is in the document or room right now — presence, not a member list.

name: realtime-chat
useWhen: A room chat needs to exist and running a separate socket service for it is not worth it.

name: realtime-cursor
useWhen: Collaboration must feel live — other people's cursors moving is the cheapest proof of that.

name: realtime-monaco
useWhen: Multiple people edit code in the same buffer and you need a working collaborative editor.

name: infinite-query-hook
useWhen: A table is too large to fetch at once and paging must stay typed against your schema.

name: platform-kit
useWhen: Your own users manage their Supabase project from inside your app — database, auth, storage, secrets, logs embedded.

name: skills
useWhen: An AI agent writes Supabase code in this repo and should follow project conventions instead of guessing RLS.

name: command-menu
useWhen: A palette is the main navigation and its open, filter, and selection motion should feel deliberate.

name: cursor
useWhen: A portfolio or campaign page replaces the system cursor to make the whole surface feel authored.

name: floating-tooltip
useWhen: The hover target is large (a map, a chart, an image) and a corner-anchored tooltip would lose the pointer.

name: glowing-badge
useWhen: One status must be visible in peripheral vision — live, recording, new — without becoming an alarm.

name: highlight
useWhen: A phrase inside a heading should be emphasised on entry rather than merely coloured.

name: kbd
useWhen: Shortcut labels sit next to this set's command menu and should share its styling.

name: magnetic-button
useWhen: The primary call to action should lean toward the cursor, making it easier to hit and harder to ignore.

name: orbiting-skills
useWhen: A CV or about page shows a tool set, and a logo cluster in orbit beats a list of badges.

name: progressive-blur
useWhen: Content must fade under a sticky header or bottom bar instead of being clipped hard.

name: scramble-text
useWhen: Technical copy should resolve out of noise, matching a terminal or security brand.

name: shimmer-skeleton
useWhen: A loading placeholder needs to look alive so slow requests do not read as frozen.

name: shimmering-text
useWhen: A label needs a light sweep for emphasis without displacing anything around it.

name: slider
useWhen: A range control in an animated context, where the stock shadcn slider would feel inert.

name: switch
useWhen: A toggle whose thumb motion should match the rest of this set.

name: text-reveal
useWhen: A statement reveals as it scrolls into view, slowing the reader down on purpose.

name: theme-switch
useWhen: Theme switching is a visible moment rather than a setting buried in a menu.

name: tilt-card
useWhen: A card should gain depth on hover, marking it as interactive in a grid of many.

name: tilt
useWhen: You want the same tilt behaviour around your own content — the primitive behind Tilt Card.

name: tooltip-preview
useWhen: A link should preview its destination, so the user can decide without navigating away.

name: velocity-highlight
useWhen: Emphasis should react to how fast the user scrolls, tying the effect to their own input.

name: copy
useWhen: A token, command, or ID is copied often and the button must confirm and reset itself.

name: glow
useWhen: The hero call to action must survive a busy or dark background.

name: refresh
useWhen: Data can be re-fetched manually and the spin must be tied to the actual request, not a fixed timeout.

name: pixel
useWhen: A retro or game-adjacent brand needs an animated pixel field behind a section.

name: clipped-circle
useWhen: A section or image reveals through an expanding circular clip, used as a transition between states.

name: count-up
useWhen: Metrics should count when they enter the viewport, so the numbers get read instead of scrolled past.

name: math-graph
useWhen: A technical page needs a plotted curve as decoration, without pulling in a charting library.
